title: Best Investment Management Software with Fund Admin Services (2027)
summary: Real-estate syndication software that accelerates capital raising. We've already helped many real-estate syndicators raise $100MM+ using Cash Flow Portal.
body_markdown:
Investment management software can raise your capital, run your waterfalls and host your investor portal. It can’t reconcile your bank accounts, close your books or answer your CPA’s questions in March. Software only goes so far if nobody is running your fund’s back office.


That is where fund administration services come in. The platforms below don’t just sell software; they also offer (or connect you with) the people who keep your books, produce NAV and capital account statements, and get your investors their K-1s on time.


We compare six options: **Cash Flow Portal, InvestNext, Agora, Juniper Square, NAV Fund Services** and **AppFolio Investment Manager** . No single platform is the best for every fund, so for each one we look at who actually does the accounting, how it’s priced relative to the others, and which market segment it fits.


**


*Disclosure: this guide is published by Cash Flow Portal. We’ve tried to describe every platform fairly, using public information and G2 ratings as of October 2026. Check pricing and features with each vendor before you decide.*


## What fund admin services should include


A fund administrator handles the back-office work that sits behind every distribution and investor statement. At a minimum, that means:


1. **Bookkeeping:** expense categorization and monthly bank reconciliations for each fund entity.
2. **Financial statements:** balance sheet and income statement on the cadence your operating agreement requires.
3. **NAV statements:** the fund’s net asset value, calculated consistently each period.
4. **LP capital account statements:** each investor’s contributions, distributions, allocations and ending balance.
5. **Tax handoff:** books prepared so your CPA can produce K-1s without weeks of cleanup.


## How we evaluated each platform


Beyond that checklist, five questions separate the options:


- **Who does the work?** In-house accountants, a partner network, or you.
- **Where is the team?** Time zones and familiarity with US partnership tax both affect how fast questions get answered.
- **Will you keep the same accountant?** Fund admin is a relationship business. A new accountant every few months means re-explaining your structure every few months.
- **Is it integrated with the software?** When the accountants work in the same system as your investor portal, capital balances don’t need to be reconciled between two vendors.
- **How does pricing scale?** Per fund, per dollar of equity under management (EUM), or a minimum tier you pay for regardless of size.


## Which market segment are you in?


The right platform depends mostly on how much equity you manage. We use five segments throughout this guide, based on equity under management (EUM):


If you’re in a smaller segment but plan to grow, pick a platform built for the segment you’re growing into, so you don’t have to switch later.


## At a glance


Cash Flow Portal, InvestNext, Agora and Juniper Square pair software with fund admin; NAV is a service firm with a portal; AppFolio is software only.


Relative cost is our own rough scale, from $ (lowest) to $$$$$ (highest). G2 ratings from[G2](https://www.g2.com/compare/agora-real-estate-vs-cash-flow-portal) as of October 2026.


## 1. Cash Flow Portal


Cash Flow Portal pairs its investment management software with a fully integrated fund admin service run by US-based accountants. The same team keeps your books, prepares NAV and LP capital account statements, and hands off to a CPA at the same firm for tax.


**What’s included:** bookkeeping, expense categorization, bank reconciliations, financial statements, NAV statements and LP capital balance statements, all visible in the same portal your investors use.


**Strengths**


- **US-based accountants** who know how to prepare partnership books so tax prep goes faster.
- **Books and taxes under one roof.** The accountants doing your books work with the CPA doing your taxes, so there’s no handoff between two firms.
- **Low staff turnover.** Customers typically keep the same accountant for years instead of re-onboarding a new one every few months.
- **Mid-range pricing ($$).** Fund admin is a per-fund add-on to the software, with no institutional minimum.
- **Flexibility.** Keep your in-house team or bring your own fund administrator and accountant.
- **Syndications and funds in one account,** including SPVs and co-GP structures.


**Trade-offs**


- Built for the middle market ($50M–$200M in EUM). Smaller managers can start here and scale up to $200M without switching platforms, but firms well past $1B may prefer an institutional platform such as Juniper Square.
- Fund admin pricing isn’t published; it’s quoted per fund.


**Best for:** middle-market sponsors ($50M–$200M), or smaller ones planning to get there, who want software and back office from one team.


## 2. InvestNext


InvestNext offers investment management software comparable to Cash Flow Portal’s, with integrated fund administration delivered through a network of vetted partner firms who work inside the platform.


**Strengths**


- Broad feature set: fundraising, investor portal, waterfalls, distributions.
- Fund admin partners work directly in InvestNext, so investor data and books stay connected.
- You can keep your current administrator; InvestNext trains them on the platform during onboarding.


**Trade-offs**


- Tiers are quote-only, fund admin is an add-on, and onboarding carries a separate migration fee.
- Because the accounting is done by partner firms, ask who will be assigned to your account and where they are based.


**Best for:** middle-market firms ($50M–$200M) that want an all-in-one platform with a choice of admin partners.


## 3. Agora


Agora pairs its software with fund administration through a co-sourcing model: fund admin partners such as Verivest work inside Agora, and Agora also sells its own bookkeeping and tax services.


**Strengths**


- A Bookkeeping Center shows the status of the books for each entity, which makes it easy to see what’s done and what’s waiting.
- Choice of admin partners, or bring your own administrator and accountant.
- Polished investor portal and fundraising tools.


**Trade-offs**


- Fund admin, bookkeeping and tax are each priced separately from the software.
- Agora’s team is split across the US, Tel Aviv and Australia, and its bookkeepers and accountants include overseas staff, which helps keep costs low. Ask which time zone your accountant works in and how complex-fund questions are escalated.


**Best for:** upper-middle-market managers ($200M–$1B) comfortable choosing among admin partners and paying for services à la carte.


## 4. Juniper Square


Juniper Square is built for institutional managers. Its in-house administration team works in the same system as the client, and the platform supports managers with over $1 billion in equity under management.


**Strengths**


- Proven at institutional scale, with large numbers of entities and LPs on the platform.
- In-house administrators on the same software, which avoids reconciling between a separate admin and your portal.


**Trade-offs**


- At the high end on cost ($$$$), with quote-only pricing and fund admin priced separately from the software.
- Because it’s built mainly for institutional clients, Juniper Square tends to quote fund admin starting at around $100M in equity under management. Smaller managers may end up paying for more capacity than they use.


**Best for:** institutional managers ($1B+) who need institutional-grade reporting.


## 5. NAV Fund Services (formerly NAV Consulting)


NAV is a traditional fund administrator that has served alternative funds since 1991. It covers bookkeeping, fund accounting, NAV and investor statements, but it is a service provider first, not GP software.


**Strengths**


- Decades of experience across fund types, including real estate.
- Tailored, all-inclusive pricing with no setup fees, plus a free white-label investor portal and mobile app.


**Trade-offs**


- The investor portal is built around accounting reports. If you want a modern portal for fundraising and investor relations, you’ll likely need separate software.
- Much of NAV’s back-office team is based in India, which can mean time-zone gaps when you have a complex fund question.
- Pricing is set per fund, so it can be harder to get a portfolio discount as you add vehicles.
- Focused on funds; if you also run deal-by-deal syndications, they likely won’t sit in the same portal.


**Best for:** simple funds that want fixed pricing from an established administrator, less so for growing multi-vehicle sponsors.


## 6. AppFolio Investment Manager


AppFolio Investment Manager is investment management software, not a fund administrator. It doesn’t provide fund admin services directly, so you would hire a separate firm (AppFolio lists accounting partners such as Armanino).


**Best for:** upper-middle-market sponsors ($200M–$1B) already running property management on AppFolio who have their own fund accountant or administrator.


## How to choose


Start with your market segment (see the table above), then check the special cases and ask every vendor the same questions.


**Special cases:**


- **One simple fund, little need for a modern portal:** a traditional administrator such as NAV.
- **Already on AppFolio for property management:** AppFolio Investment Manager plus a separate fund admin firm.


**Questions to ask on every demo:**


- Who exactly will do my books, and where are they based?
- Will I keep the same accountant year over year?
- Does your accountant work with the CPA preparing my K-1s, or is that a separate firm?
- Is fund admin priced per fund, per dollar of EUM, or with a minimum tier?
- Can I bring my own administrator later, or leave yours without switching software?


## FAQ


**What is the difference between fund administration software and fund administration services?**


Software tracks investors, capital accounts and distributions. Services are the people who keep the books, reconcile the accounts and produce NAV and capital account statements. Most growing funds need both.


**Do I need a third-party fund administrator?**


There’s often no legal requirement for a US real estate fund. But many investors, lenders and auditors expect independent books, and outsourcing is usually cheaper than hiring a full-time fund accountant.


**Can I switch fund administrators without switching software?**


On platforms that let you bring your own administrator, including Cash Flow Portal, InvestNext and Agora, yes. With a service-first firm like NAV, the portal usually goes with the administrator.


**How much does fund administration cost?**


It depends on the number of entities, investors and transactions. Ask whether pricing is per fund or based on equity under management, and whether there is a minimum tier.
